messages.author: dbdfeb22dad182f2
messages.subject: Help with lstar and plots
parts:
Good evening,

I am a PhD student who is still new to r. The first paper using LSTAR (and ESTAR) was published in our field last year (they used the "RATS" statistics program) and my co-author and I are trying to add on to their model with new variables. I have searched the vignettes, mailing list, and handout, worked and worked on it and I just cannot find the answers/figure it out.

1) We need to estimate a LSTAR model using a negative binomial distribution. Any help is greatly appreciated. Also, how do you put the upper bound to 10?

#Here is my LSTAR model. I don't think it is right.
mod.lstar <- lstar(lgtd, m=2, mL=2, mH=2)
mod.lstar
summary(mod.lstar)

#Here is just the negative binomial
nb1 <- glm.nb(lgtd ~ lag_lgdp + lpop, data = data)
summary(nb1)

2) We have a DV and three IVs that need to be in the model. I cannot figure out how to place them in.

3) I am also having a lot of trouble plotting the model. Please see attachments (screen shots) from Enders et al. 2014. The graphs with "Panel 3: By Nationality" as the title are the graphs of the equations.

4) Is ESTAR available? I cannot find it.

Thank you so much for your help. It is truly appreciated. I apologize for being such a beginner. My co-author and I will be happy to include you on our list of acknowledgements if our paper is published.

Very Respectfully,
Aaron Gold

messages.author: 8c45483022d450d5
messages.subject: Re: [tsDyn] Help with lstar and plots
parts:
Dear Aaron

I am afraid the answers will all be disapointing for you:

1) There is no functionnality for LSTAR with negative binomials, you will need to write your own functions.
To change the upper bound: this is detailed in the help file, with example:
example(LSTAR, ask=FALSE, echo=FALSE)
controls <- list(gammaInt=c(1,2000), nGamma=50)
mod.lstar3 <- lstar(log10(lynx), m=1,  include="none", starting.control=controls)
mod.lstar3


kindly let me know if you believe this is not clear and can be improved?

2) There is no functionnality for a LSTAR with dummy variables. I am not sure to have seen paper discussing this case anyway?

3) I don't see what this plot is. If you want to plot the transition function, you will have to do it manually

4) ESTAR: unfortunately not

Best

Matthieu
